text:
SRE-Bot: :rotating_light: Alert: anomalous KV cache growth observed in prod-us-east-2; continuous-batching queue depth rising for several Llama and Mistral routes. Auto-throttle triggered but latency climbed above SLOs. Root of spike unknown. thread id=2462345678

Alex: I'm paged, looking at dashboard now.

Maria: Seeing sustained prefix cardinality increase on model=llama-70b, route=/chat/stream. KV miss ratio jumped from 5% -> 42% in 3m. Continuous-batch backlog 2k requests.

Jin: Oncall here. Any recent rollout?

Alex: No deploys in last hour. We did push a config tweak to batching.service yesterday (increased max_batch_tokens for experimental routes). Could be related.

Luis: Support telemetry shows two enterprise customers on dedicated pools reporting 20–30% throughput drops and 400–800ms p99 latency rise. Ticket numbers 8342, 8343.

Maria: Correlating logs: many small prompts with repeated prefixes causing KV entries to explode. Looks like cache keys not normalizing for some Mistral variants (mistral-instruct-lite) under new batching holiday mode.

Jin: Risk: KV cache growth -> evictions -> cache churn -> more API latency. Mitigation plan: 1) throttle continuous batching for affected models, 2) apply a temporary prefix-normalization filter, 3) notify customers and open status update.

Alex: Agreed. I'll apply a conservative batching hotfix: set max_batch_tokens=512 and batch_timeout_ms=8 on routes matching llama-* and mistral-*.

Maria: Please also flip off 'prefetch_all' experimental flag for those pools. That seemed correlated in last runbooks.

Jin: Applying hotfix now. Patch command:```bash
# apply batch config via infractl
infractl route update --route-filter "model:llama-*|model:mistral-*" \
  --set max_batch_tokens=512 --set batch_timeout_ms=8 --set prefetch_all=false
```

Jin: Patch applied to prod-us-east-2 canary subset (10% nodes) at 2462345902. Monitoring.

SRE-Bot: Deploy event recorded: infractl update (change-id=chg-90821) by Jin.

Alex: Good. I'm seeing immediate drop in continuous-batch queue depth on canary nodes. KV allocation rate back to baseline in 45s.

Luis: Customer tickets update: initial acknowledgement sent. Will prepare a brief status blurb for support Slack and status page.

SupportBot: Draft for status page: "We are mitigating increased latency affecting some Llama and Mistral inference routes due to unexpected cache growth. A hotfix to batching configuration is rolling out; performance is improving for affected customers." Want approval?

Maria: Approve the copy. Add note: "No model outputs were corrupted; this was a serving performance issue."

Jin: Canary looks healthy. Rolling to 50% at 2462346050.

Alex: Observability note: KV evictions dropped from 18k/min -> 1.2k/min post-hotfix on canary. Prefetch off eliminated a bursty N+1 cache fill pattern.

Maria: Running a targeted eval on Qwen routes — there are some GQA edge cases where prompt folding produced very long prefix chains; not seeing failure but we'll add a normalization rule to the router to collapse repeated user IDs in prefix keys.

Jin: Rolling the normalization rule as a lower-priority follow-up (will not block rollback). Command:```json
{"rule":"normalize_prefixes","patterns":["user_session_id","chat_thread_id"],"strategy":"hash-truncate-64"}
```

Alex: Please log that change in changelog and add to post-incident follow-up.

Luis: Sending customer updates now. Support posted to channel #cust-notify and updated tickets 8342/8343. No customers requested escalations.

SRE-Bot: Auto-check at 2462346200: latency p99 for affected routes reduced to within SLO (was 820ms, now 180ms). Error rates stable.

Oncall Pager: Jin — handoff in 30m. Prepare a short runbook for night oncall.

Jin: Creating runbook notes: 1) watch KV allocation RPS, 2) watch continuous-batch queue depth, 3) if growth > 15% sustained for 2m, scale down prefetch and throttle batching for model set, 4) engage eng-runtime if evictions > 5k/min despite throttle.

Maria: I'll triage a root-cause ticket to infra and model-onboarding: possible key-generation drift in the model tokenizer wrapper for Mistral. Assigning to @eng-runtime and @eng-ml.

Alex: Post-incident actions: - Reproduce locally with fuzzed prefix sequences - Add unit tests for prefix normalization - Revert experimental batch increases until we have better telemetry - Update runbook with exact infractl commands used

Luis: Drafting a short postmortem outline for customers and internal review. Will include timeline, impact, mitigation, and action items.

SupportBot: Status update posted to status.redwood.ai at 2462346280.

Jin: Handing off to Maria for the night. I'm available on pager if it regresses. :thumbsup:

Maria: Taking oncall. Leaving notes in the thread and runbook. Will follow up with eng-runtime and eng-ml for permanent fix.

Alex: Thanks all. Closing incident once postmortem is ready and next-day follow-ups scheduled. :white_check_mark:
